Docs.Title: Sec. 1-1-1. - Designation and citation of the City Code and ordinances enacted under this Code.
Docs.Content:
(a)

This Code shall be designated and cited as the "2019 Detroit City Code."

(b)

After an ordinance is passed by the City Council in accordance with Section 4-108 of the Charter and approved by the Mayor in accordance with Section 4-117 of the Charter, the City Clerk shall provide a numerical designation of the ordinance for use in the Notice of Enactment for publication of the ordinance in accordance with Section 4-118 of the Charter and in the printing of the ordinance in a loose-leaf format. After enactment of the ordinance to adopt this Code, the numerical designation shall contain the year and the number of the ordinance as enacted in chronological order during each calendar year. As examples, the 35th ordinance enacted during Calendar Year 2019 shall be designated and cited as "Ord. No. 2019-35," the first ordinance enacted during Calendar Year 2020 shall be designated and cited as "Ord. No. 2020-1," and the ninth ordinance enacted during Calendar Year 2021 shall be designated and cited as "Ord. No. 2021-9."

(Code 1964, § 1-1-1; Code 1984, § 1-1-1; Ord. No. 20-97, § 1(1-1-1), eff. 7-25-1997)

Charter reference— Mandate for codification, § 4-119.

State Law reference— Authority to codify, MCL 117.5b.

Docs.Title: Sec. 1-1-2. - Definitions; rules of construction.
Docs.Content:
(a)

For the purposes of this Code, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section unless otherwise defined within the text of the provision:

Blight violation means any unlawful act, or any omission or failure to act, which is designated by this Code as a blight violation pursuant to Section 41(2) of the Michigan Home Rule City Act, being MCL 117.41(2).

Charter means, unless referred to as the 1918, 1974, or 1997 Charters, the 2012 Charter of the City of Detroit, which was adopted by the People of the City of Detroit on November 8, 2011, and became effective on January 1, 2012, and shall include any amendment to such Charter.

City means the City of Detroit, Michigan.

City Council or Council means the legislative body of the City as provided for by the Charter.

Civil infraction means an act or omission that is prohibited by this Code, which is not a crime as defined in Section 5 of the Michigan Penal Code, being MCL 750.5, and for which civil sanctions may be ordered.

Code means, unless referred to as the 1954, 1964 or 1984 Detroit City Codes, the "2019 Detroit City Code."

County means the County of Wayne, Michigan.

Criminal offense means a felony or misdemeanor as set forth in federal or state law or this Code, but does not mean a blight violation or civil infraction.

Land or real estate means real property and all of the rights and interests thereto.

Loop or loop district means that section of the City bounded on the south by the south line of East Jefferson Avenue and West Jefferson Avenue; on the east by the east line of St. Antoine Street; on the north by the north line of Columbia Street; and on the west by the west line of First Street.

Mayor means the chief executive of the City as provided for by the Charter.

MCL means the Michigan Compiled Laws.

Month means a calendar month.

One-Mile Circle means that area bounded by Vernor Highway on the north, the Chrysler Freeway on the east, the Detroit River on the south, and the John C. Lodge Freeway on the west.

Owner means, when applied to a building or land, or real estate, any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, tenant in partnership, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety of the whole or of a part of such building or land.

Person means an individual, association, firm, partnership, political body, and corporate body, or other legal entity.

Signature or subscription means a person's name written by that person or, when the person cannot write, an identifying mark made by the person.

State means the State of Michigan.

Street means avenues, boulevards, roads, alleys, lanes, viaducts, and all other public highways and thoroughfares in the City.

Tenant or occupant means a person who has a written or oral lease of, or who occupies, the whole or a part of a building or land, either alone or with others.

(b)

In the construction of this Code, the following rules of construction shall apply, unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the Charter or this Code:

Agency. Any mention of any City, state, or federal agency shall include any successor agency.

Computation of time. Unless otherwise specifically provided, the time within which an act is required by this Code to be done shall be computed by excluding the first day and including the last day. If the last day on which the time period runs is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the time period runs until the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday.

Case law annotation—This code of construction constitutes an effective waiver of strict compliance with a statute requiring notice of damage claims against the City within a certain time. Murphy v Detroit, 2 Mich App 473; 140 NW2d 565 (1966). (This case construed similar language in this section contained in the 1964 Code).

Gender. The terms of one gender shall include the other gender as well as the neuter gender.

Generally. When provisions conflict, the specific shall prevail over the general. All provisions shall be liberally construed so that the intent of the City Council may be effectuated. Terms and phrases shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but technical terms, technical phrases, and terms and phrases that have acquired peculiar and appropriate meanings in law shall be construed according to such meanings.

Oath shall be construed to include the term "affirmation" in all cases where, by this Code or practice, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath.

Office, department, commission, or other City agency. Whenever any office, department, commission or other City agency is referred to by title only, such reference shall be construed as if followed by the words "of the City of Detroit, Michigan."

Officer. Whenever, by the provisions of this Code, any officer of the City is assigned any duty or empowered to perform any act or duty, reference to such officer shall mean and include such officer or such officer's deputy or authorized subordinate.

Plural includes the singular.

Public act. Any reference to a public act, whether by act number or by short title, is a reference to the act as amended, or any successor statute.

Singular includes the plural.

Sworn includes the term "affirmed" in all cases where, by this Code or practice, an affirmation may be substituted for a swearing.

(Code 1964, § 1-1-2; Code 1984, § 1-1-2; Ord. No. 20-97, § 1(1-1-2), eff. 7-25-1997)

State Law reference— Statutory rules of construction, MCL 8.3 et seq.

Docs.Content:
The chapter, article, and division headings, the section catchlines and history notes, and all references and notes that are contained within this Code shall be of no legal import and are provided only to assist in the usage of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 1-1-3; Code 1984, § 1-1-3; Ord. No. 20-97, § 1(1-1-3), eff. 7-25-1997)
